speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help you with your wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions, I need to understand the nature of these symptoms first. How would you describe the skin lesions, and when did they first appear?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Disease (Borrelia burgdorferi infection)

The combination of recent camping in Minnesota, a self-resolving knee pain (suggestive of early oligoarticular Lyme arthritis), and current monoarticular wrist pain with systemic symptoms is highly suspicious for Lyme disease. While sexually active, the epidemiological clues point more strongly toward a tick-borne illness. I will proceed with a diagnosis based on this clinical picture.
